source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Pinned Greek read completely before authoring. Matthew 24–25 prior Fluent consulted after Greek reading, before final wording; Matthew 26–28 drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW compared programmatically after authoring, not used as a base. Every verse carries a source-specific decision. No word-change quota.

verses.rationale: Connects the participial departure to the disciples’ approach in one natural sentence.
verses.before: Jesus left the temple and was going away when his disciples came to point out the temple buildings to him.
verses.after: Jesus was leaving the temple when his disciples came over to show him its buildings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus left the temple and was going away, when his disciples came to point out to him the buildings of the temple.

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic total destruction without stacking English negatives.
verses.before: He answered them, “Do you see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
verses.after: He replied, “Do you see all this? I tell you the truth: not one stone here will remain on another. Every one will be torn down.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he answered them, “Do you see all these things? Truly, I say to you, there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down.”

verses.rationale: Separates the approach from two questions while retaining coming and age language.
verses.before: As Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately and asked, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the completion of the age?”
verses.after: As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will this happen? What will be the sign of your coming and the end of the age?”
verses.tsw_comparator: As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”

verses.rationale: Makes the warning idiomatic without narrowing deception to one group.
verses.before: Jesus answered them, “See that no one leads you astray.
verses.after: Jesus answered, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus answered them, “See that no one leads you astray.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated many and the messianic claim.
verses.before: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray.
verses.after: Many will come in my name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray.

verses.rationale: Makes the warning audible in short sentences and retains the not-yet qualification.
verses.before: You will hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, because these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
verses.after: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. Do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end has not yet come.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for this must take place, but the end is not yet.

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel conflicts while separating the list of disasters.
verses.before: Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
verses.after: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
verses.tsw_comparator: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

verses.rationale: Retains the childbirth metaphor without interpreting its timetable.
verses.before: All these things are the beginning of birth pains.
verses.after: All this is the beginning of birth pains.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these are but the beginning of birth pains.

verses.rationale: Replaces the unnatural hand-over-to-distress phrase while preserving persecution and motive.
verses.before: Then they will hand you over to distress and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.
verses.after: “Then they will hand you over to suffering and kill you. All nations will hate you because of my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they will deliver you up to tribulation and put you to death, and you will be hated by all nations for my name’s sake.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three linked actions and reciprocal betrayal.
verses.before: Then many will fall away, hand one another over, and hate one another.
verses.after: At that time many will fall away, hand one another over, and hate one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: And then many will fall away and betray one another and hate one another.

verses.rationale: Retains clear wording and the repeated many.
verses.before: Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
verses.after: Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: And many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.

verses.rationale: Expresses the causal development while retaining the cold-love image.
verses.before: Because lawlessness will increase, the love of many will grow cold.
verses.after: As lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
verses.tsw_comparator: And because lawlessness will be increased, the love of many will grow cold.

verses.rationale: Retains endurance and salvation without specifying an unstated mechanism.
verses.before: But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
verses.after: But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

verses.rationale: Preserves world and nations as distinct expressions and separates the final consequence.
verses.before: And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
verses.after: This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the inhabited world as a testimony to all nations. Then the end will come.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

verses.rationale: Retains the scriptural expression and narrator’s reader-directed aside.
verses.before: “Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
verses.after: “So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
verses.tsw_comparator: “So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—

verses.rationale: Connects the command naturally to the preceding when-clause.
verses.before: then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
verses.after: those in Judea must flee to the mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rooftop setting and urgent prohibition in ordinary English.
verses.before: Let the one on the housetop not come down to take things out of the house,
verses.after: Anyone on the roof must not go down to collect things from the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the one who is on the housetop not go down to take what is in his house,

verses.rationale: Retains the specific garment and urgency without extra explanation.
verses.before: and let the one in the field not turn back to get a cloak.
verses.after: Anyone in the field must not turn back for a cloak.
verses.tsw_comparator: and let the one who is in the field not turn back to take his cloak.

verses.rationale: Expresses the lament as compassion for the specified women.
verses.before: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those nursing infants in those days!
verses.after: How terrible those days will be for pregnant women and nursing mothers!
verses.tsw_comparator: And alas for women who are pregnant and for those who are nursing infants in those days!

verses.rationale: Makes flight verbal while preserving Matthew’s Sabbath detail.
verses.before: Pray that your flight will not happen in winter or on a Sabbath.
verses.after: Pray that you will not have to flee in winter or on a Sabbath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on a Sabbath.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unmatched distress and both temporal limits.
verses.before: For then there will be great distress, unlike anything from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be repeated.
verses.after: For then there will be great suffering, unlike anything since the world began, and never to be repeated.
verses.tsw_comparator: For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, and never will be.

verses.rationale: Renders no-flesh-saved naturally in the threat to survival; retains chosen language.
verses.before: If those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be cut short.
verses.after: If those days were not cut short, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be cut short.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the elect those days will be cut short.

verses.rationale: Preserves both competing location claims and the prohibition.
verses.before: “Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘There he is!’ do not believe it.
verses.after: “If anyone then tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There he is!’ do not believe it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There he is!’ do not believe it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the if-possible qualification without resolving its implications.
verses.before: For false christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders in order to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
verses.after: False christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
verses.tsw_comparator: For false christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect.

verses.rationale: Renders the attention marker as a reminder of the advance warning.
verses.before: Look, I have told you beforehand.
verses.after: Remember, I have warned you beforehand.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, I have told you beforehand.

verses.rationale: Separates the two conditional warnings for listening clarity.
verses.before: Therefore if they tell you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or, ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
verses.after: So if they tell you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out. If they say, ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
verses.tsw_comparator: So if they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out. If they say, ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the visible lightning comparison and established title.
verses.before: For just as lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
verses.after: For as lightning flashes from east to west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

verses.rationale: Retains the unexplained proverb and corpse rather than interpreting it.
verses.before: Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.
verses.after: Wherever the corpse is, the vultures will gather.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.

verses.rationale: Lineates the scriptural cosmic imagery without turning it into a modern explanation.
verses.before: “Immediately after the distress of those days, ‘the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’
verses.after: “Immediately after the suffering of those days, ‘the sun will be darkened, and the moon will give no light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

verses.rationale: Retains the ambiguous sign phrase, tribal mourning, and cloud imagery.
verses.before: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
verses.after: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then will appear in heaven the sign of the Son of Man, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

verses.rationale: Keeps angels, trumpet, and four winds rather than replacing them with explanations.
verses.before: He will send his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
verses.after: He will send his angels with a mighty trumpet, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he will send out his angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

verses.rationale: Makes the lesson introduction idiomatic while retaining the seasonal observation.
verses.before: “Learn the parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
verses.after: “Learn this lesson from the fig tree: when its branches grow tender and put out leaves, you know summer is near.
verses.tsw_comparator: “From the fig tree learn its lesson: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer is near.

verses.rationale: Keeps it/he ambiguity in a note rather than specifying an event in the text.
verses.before: In the same way, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
verses.after: In the same way, when you see all these things, know that it is near, right at the door.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also, when you see all these things, you know that he is near, at the very gates.

verses.rationale: Retains this generation without changing it to a future generation or people.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
verses.after: I tell you the truth: this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly, I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.

verses.rationale: Carries the emphatic negation through never while retaining the parallel.
verses.before: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
verses.after: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

verses.rationale: Preserves nor the Son in the pinned Greek without theological adjustment.
verses.before: “But concerning that day and hour no one knows—not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but the Father alone.
verses.after: “But no one knows that day or hour—not the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But concerning that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but the Father only.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the comparison’s English syntax while retaining the title.
verses.before: For just as the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
verses.after: As it was in the days of Noah, so it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as were the days of Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

verses.rationale: Retains both marriage actions and ordinary activities without moralizing them.
verses.before: In those days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
verses.after: In the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day when Noah entered the ark,

verses.rationale: Preserves ignorance and sudden removal without assigning roles to later taken/left sayings.
verses.before: They did not know until the flood came and swept them all away. So also will be the coming of the Son of Man.
verses.after: They knew nothing until the flood came and swept them all away. So it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they were unaware until the flood came and swept them all away, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

verses.rationale: Supplies people for natural English without specifying their fate.
verses.before: Then two will be in the field; one will be taken and one left.
verses.after: Then two people will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then two men will be in the field; one will be taken and one left.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicitly female workers and parallel taken/left wording.
verses.before: Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and one left.
verses.after: Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and the other left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and one left.

verses.rationale: Keeps the watchfulness image and day language.
verses.before: Therefore stay awake, because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
verses.after: So stay awake, because you do not know what day your Lord will come.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, stay awake, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.

verses.rationale: Renders night-watch timing naturally; preserves the hypothetical householder.
verses.before: But understand this: if the owner of the house had known at what watch the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.after: Understand this: if the homeowner had known what time of night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.
verses.tsw_comparator: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what part of the night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.

verses.rationale: Retains unexpected timing without supplying a date or sequence.
verses.before: Therefore you also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
verses.after: You too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore you also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.

verses.rationale: Makes the household responsibility explicit while preserving servant status in vocabulary.
verses.before: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant whom the master put over the household to give them food at the proper time?
verses.after: “Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom the master has put in charge of his household to give them food at the proper time?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his master has set over his household, to give them their food at the proper time?

verses.rationale: Clarifies the antecedent of doing so and the master’s return.
verses.before: Blessed is that servant whom the master finds doing so when he comes.
verses.after: Blessed is that servant if his master finds him doing this when he returns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is that servant whom his master will find so doing when he comes.

verses.rationale: Makes the promised responsibility idiomatic.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, the master will put that servant over all his possessions.
verses.after: I tell you the truth: he will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly, I say to you, he will set him over all his possessions.

verses.rationale: Renders speech in the heart as internal speech and delay idiomatically.
verses.before: But if that evil servant says in his heart, ‘My master is delayed,’
verses.after: But suppose that wicked servant says to himself, ‘My master is taking a long time,’
verses.tsw_comparator: But if that wicked servant says to himself, ‘My master is delayed,’

verses.rationale: Preserves abuse of fellow servants and the second pattern of conduct.
verses.before: and begins to beat fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards,
verses.after: and begins beating his fellow servants and eating and drinking with drunkards.
verses.tsw_comparator: and begins to beat his fellow servants and eats and drinks with drunkards,

verses.rationale: Removes a nested possessive while retaining both time expressions.
verses.before: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect and at an hour he does not know.
verses.after: That servant’s master will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know.
verses.tsw_comparator: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know

verses.rationale: Retains the violent judgment and recurring final image without softening it.
verses.before: He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
verses.after: He will cut him in two and give him a place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and will cut him in pieces and put him with the hypocrites. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.rationale: Retains the wedding setting and kingdom comparison; virgins identified in vocabulary.
verses.before: “Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
verses.after: “Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

verses.rationale: Retains the balanced division in a concise sentence.
verses.before: Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
verses.after: Five were foolish and five were wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

verses.rationale: Makes the contrast compact without inserting extra oil into the main text.
verses.before: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take oil with them.
verses.after: The foolish ones brought their lamps but no oil with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when the foolish took their lamps, they took no oil with them,

verses.rationale: Renders containers concretely while preserving the additional supply.
verses.before: The wise ones took oil in containers along with their lamps.
verses.after: The wise ones brought jars of oil along with their lamps.
verses.tsw_comparator: but the wise took flasks of oil with their lamps.

verses.rationale: Retains all ten sleeping; does not turn foolishness into sleep alone.
verses.before: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
verses.after: The bridegroom was delayed, and they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.

verses.rationale: Makes the sudden midnight cry natural without adding the absent comes verb.
verses.before: But at midnight there was a shout: ‘Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’
verses.after: At midnight a shout rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’
verses.tsw_comparator: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’

verses.rationale: Renders preparation broadly rather than specifying wick-trimming as certain.
verses.before: Then all the bridesmaids got up and trimmed their lamps.
verses.after: Then all the bridesmaids got up and put their lamps in order.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps.

verses.rationale: Keeps the request and immediate reason together.
verses.before: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.’
verses.after: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And the foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the concern about sufficiency and direct instruction without adding a moral verdict.
verses.before: But the wise answered, ‘There may not be enough for both us and you. Go instead to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’
verses.after: But the wise ones answered, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But the wise answered, saying, ‘Since there will not be enough for us and for you, go rather to the dealers and buy for yourselves.’

verses.rationale: Clarifies the simultaneous action and retains the shut door.
verses.before: While they were going to buy it, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
verses.after: While they were away buying oil, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
verses.tsw_comparator: And while they were going to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

verses.rationale: Gives the repeated address audible dialogue without changing it to the narrator’s endorsement.
verses.before: Later the other bridesmaids also came and said, ‘Lord, lord, open for us!’
verses.after: Later the other bridesmaids came too. ‘Lord, lord,’ they said, ‘open the door for us!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward the other virgins came also, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open to us.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the denial of recognition and solemn introductory formula.
verses.before: But he answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
verses.after: But he replied, ‘I tell you the truth: I do not know you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But he answered, ‘Truly, I say to you, I do not know you.’

verses.rationale: Marks the return from parable dialogue to Jesus’ warning without adding a source-absent clause.
verses.before: Therefore stay awake, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
verses.after: “So stay awake, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, stay awake, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

verses.rationale: Divides the journey setup from the entrusted responsibility without redefining the comparison.
verses.before: “It is also like a man going on a journey who called his servants and entrusted his possessions to them.
verses.after: “It is also like a man about to travel. He called his servants and entrusted his property to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For it will be like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted to them his property.

verses.rationale: Keeps the large monetary unit and the source position of immediately, continuing into the next verse.
verses.before: To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to ability. Then he went away.
verses.after: He gave one five talents, another two, and another one, each according to his ability. Then he left. At once,
verses.tsw_comparator: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his ability. Then he went away.

verses.rationale: Joins at-once to the servant’s action across the verse boundary.
verses.before: The one who received five talents went immediately, traded with them, and gained five more.
verses.after: the servant who received five talents went to work with them and gained five more.
verses.tsw_comparator: He who had received the five talents went at once and traded with them, and he made five talents more.

verses.rationale: Retains the parallel gain and relative amounts.
verses.before: In the same way, the one with two gained two more.
verses.after: In the same way, the servant with two gained two more.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also he who had the two talents made two talents more.

verses.rationale: Makes the sequence concrete and keeps money rather than innate talent.
verses.before: But the one who received one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master's money.
verses.after: But the servant who received one went off, dug a hole, and hid his master’s money in the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he who had received the one talent went and dug in the ground and hid his master’s money.

verses.rationale: Retains the lengthy delay and financial reckoning.
verses.before: After a long time, the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.
verses.after: After a long time, the servants’ master returned and settled accounts with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.

verses.rationale: Clarifies speaker and action while retaining the repeated amounts.
verses.before: The one who had received five talents came and brought five more, saying, ‘Master, you entrusted me with five talents. Look, I gained five more.’
verses.after: The servant who had received five talents came forward with five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted five talents to me. Look, I have gained five more.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And he who had received the five talents came forward, bringing five talents more, saying, ‘Master, you delivered to me five talents; here I have made five talents more.’

verses.rationale: Makes entering joy idiomatic without replacing it with a specified reward.

verses.tsw_comparator: and twisting together a crown of thorns, they put it on his head and put a reed in his right hand. And kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Judeans!”

verses.rationale: Keeps all three abusive actions without embellishment.
verses.before: They spit on him, took the reed, and kept striking him on the head.
verses.after: They spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on the head.
verses.tsw_comparator: They spat on him and took the reed and struck him on the head.

verses.before: After mocking him, they took off the cloak, put his own clothes back on him, and led him away to crucify him.
verses.after: When they had finished mocking him, they removed the cloak, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him away to crucify him.

verses.rationale: Retains origin, name, and coercion without inventing Simon’s motivation.

verses.after: As they went out, they came upon a man from Cyrene named Simon and forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.

verses.rationale: Preserves the place name and the narrator’s explanation.
verses.before: When they came to a place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull,
verses.after: They came to a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.”

verses.rationale: Retains gall rather than importing Mark’s myrrh.

verses.after: They offered Jesus wine mixed with gall. After tasting it, he refused to drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves the casting of lots without inserting a source-absent fulfillment quotation.

verses.after: After crucifying him, they divided his clothes by casting lots.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments among them by casting lots.

verses.rationale: Retains the soldiers’ watch at the execution site.
verses.before: Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.
verses.after: Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete inscription and its function as charge.

verses.after: Above his head they placed the written charge against him: “This is Jesus, the king of the Jews.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And over his head they put the charge against him, which read, “This is Jesus, the King of the Judeans.”

verses.rationale: Retains the two companions and their positions without characterizing their later responses differently.

verses.after: Two bandits were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then two rebels were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.

verses.rationale: Keeps verbal and bodily mockery connected to the following speech.
verses.before: Those passing by reviled him, shaking their heads
verses.after: Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads
verses.tsw_comparator: And those who passed by derided him, wagging their heads

verses.rationale: Preserves the challenge’s conditional wording and its sanctuary accusation.
verses.before: and saying, “You who would destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are God's Son, come down from the cross!”
verses.after: and saying, “You who would destroy the sanctuary and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are God’s Son, come down from the cross!”
verses.tsw_comparator: and saying, “You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the specified group as the next speakers.
verses.before: In the same way, the chief priests with the scribes and elders mocked him:
verses.after: Likewise the chief priests, with the scribes and elders, mocked him, saying,
verses.tsw_comparator: So also the chief priests, with the scribes and elders, mocked him, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains save repeated and the taunting condition for belief.
verses.before: “He saved others, but he cannot save himself! He is Israel's king. Let him come down now from the cross, and we will trust in him.
verses.after: “He saved others; he cannot save himself! He is the king of Israel. Let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the scriptural echo and the if-he-wants-him ambiguity.
verses.before: He trusted in God; let God rescue him now, if God wants him. For he said, ‘I am God's Son.’”
verses.after: He trusts in God. Let God rescue him now, if he wants him, for he said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”

verses.rationale: Retains Matthew’s plural without importing another Gospel’s repentant individual.
verses.before: In the same way, the robbers crucified with him also insulted him.
verses.after: The bandits crucified with him also insulted him in the same way.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the rebels who were crucified with him also reviled him in the same way.

verses.rationale: Renders the sixth-to-ninth hours naturally while leaving land/earth range in a note.

verses.tsw_comparator: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.

verses.rationale: Retains Matthew’s transliteration and quoted lament without explaining away abandonment.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hearers’ misunderstanding as their speech.

verses.after: Some of those standing there heard him and said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And some of the bystanders, hearing it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”

verses.rationale: Retains the urgent sequence and distinguishes sour wine from earlier gall mixture.

verses.after: Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and offered him a drink.

verses.rationale: Keeps the waiting taunt without adding the spear variant absent from the pinned text.

verses.after: The others said, “Leave him alone. Let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the others said, “Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to save him.”

verses.rationale: Retains repeated cry and spirit idiom rather than adding an explanation of his death.

verses.after: Jesus cried out loudly once more and gave up his spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and yielded up his spirit.

verses.tsw_comparator: and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection they went into the holy city and appeared to many.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shared confession and military witnesses.

verses.after: When the centurion and those guarding Jesus with him saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were terrified. “This man truly was God’s Son!” they said.

verses.rationale: Retains the women’s continued presence and prior service.

verses.after: Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and cared for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were also many women there, looking on from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three identifications without supplying the third woman’s name.
verses.before: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
verses.after: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.

verses.rationale: Retains wealth, origin, and discipleship without importing council membership.

verses.after: When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too had become a disciple of Jesus.

verses.after: He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate ordered it to be given to him.

verses.after: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.

verses.rationale: Retains Matthew’s calendar phrasing and the changed group of authorities.

verses.rationale: Keeps deceiver inside their accusation and preserves the quoted prediction.

verses.after: “Sir,” they said, “we remember that while that deceiver was still alive, he said, ‘After three days I will be raised.’
verses.tsw_comparator: and said, “Sir, we remember how that deceiver said, while he was still alive, ‘After three days I will rise.’

verses.rationale: Retains their feared scenario as a claim, not narrator fact.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ambiguous have-a-guard wording; imperative alternative goes in a note.
verses.before: Pilate told them, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you know how.”
verses.after: Pilate told them, “You have a guard. Go and secure it as best you know how.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pilate said to them, “You have a guard; go, make it as secure as you know how.”

verses.rationale: Makes the securing actions readable without elaborating the seal’s physical form.
verses.before: So they went and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone and posting the guard.
verses.after: They went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone and posting the guard.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they went and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone and setting the guard.

verses.rationale: Preserves Matthew’s two named visitors and stated purpose without importing spices.
verses.before: After the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb.
verses.after: After the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.

verses.rationale: Retains the causal connection and the angel’s actions without claiming the stone released Jesus.

verses.rationale: Preserves both similes without specifying human ethnicity.
verses.before: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
verses.after: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
verses.tsw_comparator: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.

verses.rationale: Retains the fear response and death comparison.

verses.after: The guards shook with fear of him and became like dead men.
verses.tsw_comparator: And for fear of him the guards trembled and became like dead men.

verses.rationale: Keeps reassurance addressed to the women and identifies the crucified Jesus.

verses.tsw_comparator: He is not here, for he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.

verses.rationale: Retains the commission, place, promised sight, and angel’s closing reminder.

verses.after: Then go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has been raised from the dead and is going ahead of you into Galilee. You will see him there.’ Remember, I have told you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then go quickly and tell his disciples that he has been raised from the dead, and look—he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him. Look—I have told you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves simultaneous fear and joy and the women’s urgent action.

verses.rationale: Retains the physical encounter, greeting, and worship action.
